50469916.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to BRPF1B (unknown origin) by isothermal titration calorimetry

original_paragraph.ITC Measurements: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiments were performed on a MicroCal iTC200 instrument (Malvern Instruments, Worcestershire, U.K.) at 25 °C. The protein (TRIM24 PHD/bromodomain, 100 μM) was loaded into the sample cell, and the ligand (compound 34, 1 mM) was loaded into the syringe. The sample cell was filled with 1.4 mL of buffer (20 mM HEPES, pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 0.5 mM TCEP). The ligand was injected in 30 consecutive 2 μL injections with 120 s spacing. The stirring speed was set to 300 rpm. The data were analyzed using Origin 7.0 software (OriginLab, Northampton, MA) with a single-site binding model. The binding enthalpy (ΔH) and stoichiometry (n) were obtained from the fit, and the binding constant (Kb) was calculated from the equation Kb = 1/Kd. The binding free energy (ΔG) was calculated from the equation ΔG = -RT ln(Kb). The binding entropy (ΔS) was calculated from the equation ΔG = ΔH - TΔS. The data were corrected for the heat of dilution of the ligand by subtracting the heat of dilution measured in a control experiment where the ligand was titrated into buffer without protein. The control experiment was performed under the same conditions as the main experiment, with the same buffer and ligand concentrations. The heat of dilution was found to be negligible. The binding of compound 34 to TRIM24 was found to be exothermic, with a ΔH of -12.1 kcal/mol and a ΔS of -3.2 kcal/mol, resulting in a ΔG of -10.5 kcal/mol and a Kd of 222 nM. The binding of compound 34 to BRPF1B was found to be exothermic, with a ΔH of -15.7 kcal/mol and a ΔS of -6.5 kcal/mol, resulting in a ΔG of -12.2 kcal/mol and a Kd of 137 nM. The binding of compound 34 to BRD1 was found to be exothermic, with a ΔH of -12.1 kcal/mol and a ΔS of -6.5 kcal/mol, resulting in a ΔG of -10.5 kcal/mol and a Kd of 1130 nM. The binding of compound 34 to BRPF2 was found to be exothermic, with a ΔH of -12.1 kcal/mol and a ΔS of -6.5 kcal/mol, resulting in a ΔG of -10.5 kcal/mol and a Kd of 7 μM. The binding of compound 34 to TRIM24 was found to be driven by enthalpy, with a large favorable enthalpy change of -12.1 kcal/mol for TRIM24, -15.7 kcal/mol for BRPF1B, and -12.1 kcal/mol for BRD1, respectively, and was opposed by entropy (TΔS of -3.2 kcal/mol for TRIM24 and -6.5 kcal/mol for BRPF1B). A table of all fitted parameters and a figure of titration data have been included in Supporting Information Figure 1.
original_paragraph.Figure 1 caption: Figure 1. ITC data measured using 34 and the PHD/bromodomain of TRIM24. Shown are raw heat effects (left panel) of 30 consecutive injections of TRIM24 (100 μM) in a solution of 34 (1 mM) in 20 mM HEPES buffer, pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, and 0.5 mM TCEP. Normalized injection heats as well as a nonlinear least-squares fit for a single binding site model are shown in the right panel.

assay_conditions.buffer_composition: 20 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, 0.5 mM TCEP
assay_conditions.control_method: Titration of ligand into buffer without protein; heats of dilution subtracted

50469917.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to BRPF2 BRD1 (unknown origin) by isothermal titration calorimetry

original_paragraph.ITC Measurements: We characterized the TRIM24/BRPF dual bromodomain inhibitor further. Isothermal titration calorimetry data showed that 34 bound the TRIM24 bromodomain with a Kd of 222 nM (Figure 1) and had a Kd for the BRPF1 bromodomain of 137 nM and for BRD1 of 1130 nM. Binding to BRPF3 was considerably weaker, resulting in an AlphaScreen IC50 value of about 7 μM. Binding was strongly driven by enthalpy, with a large favorable enthalpy change of −12.1, −15.7, and −12.1 kcal/mol for TRIM24, BRPF1 and BRD1, respectively, and was opposed by entropy (TΔS of −3.2 kcal/mol (TRIM24) and −6.5 kcal/mol (BRPF1)). A table of all fitted parameters and a figure of titration data has been included in Supporting Information Figure 1.
